# Finding ∫ exp(x)*cos(x) dx

## Integration by Parts (Applied Twice)

Let **I** = ∫ exp(x)*cos(x) dx

**First integration by parts:**
- u = cos(x), dv = exp(x)dx
- du = -sin(x)dx, v = exp(x)

$$I = \text{exp}(x)\cdot\cos(x) + \int \text{exp}(x)\cdot\sin(x)\,dx$$

**Second integration by parts** on ∫ exp(x)sin(x)dx:
- u = sin(x), dv = exp(x)dx
- du = cos(x)dx, v = exp(x)

$$\int \text{exp}(x)\cdot\sin(x)\,dx = \text{exp}(x)\cdot\sin(x) - \int \text{exp}(x)\cdot\cos(x)\,dx = \text{exp}(x)\cdot\sin(x) - I$$

## Solving for I

Substituting back:

$$I = \text{exp}(x)\cdot\cos(x) + \text{exp}(x)\cdot\sin(x) - I$$

$$2I = \text{exp}(x)\cdot\cos(x) + \text{exp}(x)\cdot\sin(x)$$

$$I = \frac{\text{exp}(x)\cdot(\cos(x) + \sin(x))}{2} + C$$

## Verification

Differentiating:
$$\frac{d}{dx}\left[\frac{\text{exp}(x)(\cos(x)+\sin(x))}{2}\right] = \frac{\text{exp}(x)(\cos(x)+\sin(x)) + \text{exp}(x)(-\sin(x)+\cos(x))}{2} = \text{exp}(x)\cdot\cos(x) \checkmark$$

<answer>exp(x)*(cos(x) + sin(x))/2 + C</answer>

I = ∫exp(x)*cos(x) dx

First integration by parts:
Let u = cos(x), dv = exp(x)dx
Then du = -sin(x)dx, v = exp(x)

I = exp(x)*cos(x) - ∫exp(x)*(-sin(x))dx
I = exp(x)*cos(x) + ∫exp(x)*sin(x)dx

Now for ∫exp(x)*sin(x)dx, use integration by parts again:
Let u = sin(x), dv = exp(x)dx
Then du = cos(x)dx, v = exp(x)

∫exp(x)*sin(x)dx = exp(x)*sin(x) - ∫exp(x)*cos(x)dx
= exp(x)*sin(x) - I

So substituting back:
I = exp(x)*cos(x) + exp(x)*sin(x) - I

2I = exp(x)*cos(x) + exp(x)*sin(x)

I = exp(x)*(cos(x) + sin(x))/2 + C

Let me verify by differentiating:
d/dx [exp(x)*(cos(x) + sin(x))/2]
= (1/2)*[exp(x)*(cos(x) + sin(x)) + exp(x)*(-sin(x) + cos(x))]
= (1/2)*[exp(x)*cos(x) + exp(x)*sin(x) - exp(x)*sin(x) + exp(x)*cos(x)]
= (1/2)*[2*exp(x)*cos(x)]
= exp(x)*cos(x) ✓

So the answer is exp(x)*(cos(x) + sin(x))/2 + C
